name: The Mentor
description: Warm and educational. Explains the why, celebrates progress, protects recovery, and adjusts conservatively.

safety-hr-ceiling: Heart rate is very high at {{bpm}} bpm — let's bring the effort down right away.
{{bpm}} bpm is higher than we want. Ease off now; there's no fitness up there.
data-quality-hr: Your HR signal looks unreliable, so I'll coach off power for now — maybe check the strap after the ride.
erg-spiral: Cadence is slipping — shift and spin up before the trainer makes this harder than it needs to be.
Let's lift that cadence back up; low revs at this force will snowball.
pacing-under: A touch under target — smoothly bring it back to {{watts}} W.
Power's drifted low. Find {{watts}} W again, nice and steady.
pacing-over: You're riding above target — ease back to {{watts}} W and save it for later.
A little enthusiastic! Settle back to {{watts}} W.
recovery-intent-over: Remember, today is about recovery — going harder now just borrows from tomorrow. Ease up.
Easy days make hard days possible. Back it off a touch.
fatigue-band-1: I'm seeing some fatigue building — nothing alarming, just keep the pedaling smooth and the recoveries genuinely easy.
Fatigue is creeping in. Stay relaxed and let the recoveries do their job.
fatigue-band-2: Fatigue is getting high. It's smart, not weak, to ease the next interval — quality beats quantity.
You've done good work, but the strain is showing. Consider easing off or extending the next recovery.
hr-above-expected: Heart rate is a bit higher than I'd expect for this power — could be heat or hydration. Keep an eye on it.
HR is running warm for this effort. No panic, just something to watch.
recovery-incomplete: Heart rate isn't coming down much — soft-pedal, deep breaths, let it settle.
Give yourself a real recovery here: lighter gear, easy spin, breathe.
cadence-low: Cadence has dropped below your natural rhythm — try spinning it back up; it saves your legs.
Let's find that smooth cadence again — lighter gear, quicker feet.
slot-interval-start: Here we go: {{duration}} at {{watts}} W. Settle in early and it'll feel easier.
slot-interval-start-set: Interval {{blockNumber}} of {{blockCount}}: {{duration}} at {{watts}} W. You know what to do.
slot-final-60: Final minute — you've done the hard part, just hold this.
One minute left. Stay smooth, stay strong.
slot-last-interval: Last interval! Everything you've got left — you've earned this finish.
This is the one that counts. Finish it proud.
slot-halfway: Halfway through this block — nicely done so far, just keep it steady.
Half done. Settle in, stay smooth, the back half always goes faster.

adjust_intensity_up: You're handling this beautifully — shall we add {{percent}}% and get a bit more from the session?
Everything looks controlled. A {{percent}}% bump would optimize the stimulus.
adjust_intensity_up_rationale: Stable power, steady cadence, and minimal HR drift mean you have capacity to spare today. A small increase maximizes the adaptation without risking the rest of the session.
adjust_intensity_down: Let's be smart here — dropping {{percent}}% keeps the quality high.
Today's a bit harder than planned. {{percent}}% down protects the work you've already banked.
adjust_intensity_down_rationale: HR drift says the current load exceeds what your body has today. Reducing now preserves the remaining intervals — fitness is built by finishing well, not by suffering.
extend_recovery: Recovery is where you actually get stronger — let's take {{seconds}} more seconds.
Your HR is still elevated. {{seconds}} extra seconds will make the next one count.
extend_recovery_rationale: Incomplete recovery means the next interval starts in a hole. Extra time now buys quality later.
skip_remaining_on_intervals: You've captured the training benefit — let's call the intervals and cool down well.
skip_remaining_on_intervals_rationale: Power decline plus rising HR says the productive work is done. Stopping now protects tomorrow.

completion: Great session! The consistency you showed today is exactly how fitness gets built.
Well done. Recover properly — that's where today's work becomes strength.
Solid work today. Small, repeated efforts like this are what change you as a rider.
